1. By way of the present application filed by Smt. Lipika David (hereinafter referred as ''the aggrieved'') under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against her husband Sh. Victor David (hereinafter referred as "the respondent"), CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 1 of 10 the aggrieved has sought Protection order under Section 18; Residence Order under Section 19; Monetary Relief under Section 20; Custody of minor child Violet David under Section 21 and compensation/ damages under Section 22 of the Act.
2. Briefly stated, it is the grievance of the aggrieved that after her marriage to the respondent on 20.11.2002 according to Christian Rites and Customs, they started living together as husband and wife but the respondent used to have extra marital relations with other women and when the aggrieved objected for the same, she was abused and beaten up by him.

It is also alleged that the respondent works as a A. C. Mechanic and that he had also gone abroad and earned a substantial Cc No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David vs . Sh. Victor David Page No. 1 Of 10 on 7 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28340180/
1 amount of money but did not give a penny of it to the aggrieved rather he used to sent the money to his elder brother Eric Franklin David.

sentences.text: 3. It is further alleged that respondent used to create troubles in the family under the influence liquor and that he also threatened to commit suicide and to put the blame on the aggrieved.

It is further alleged that on 03.04.2011 respondent left the house without informing the aggrieved in respect of which the aggrieved lodged a missing complaint with PS Sarojini Nagar and that the respondent was recovered by the police and sent back to the aggrieved.
It is also alleged that respondent is in the habit of inflicting injuries on himself.

4. It is alleged that in 2003 aggrieved suffered a miscarriage due to stress and physical abuse by the respondent and when in 2005 the CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 2 of 10 aggrieved again conceived, she had to bear all the expenses of medicines and hospitalization with the help of her parents.

entities.text: CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is alleged that for ten years the aggrieved has been abused and tortured physically by the respondent, however, the aggrieved after being fed up with the behaviour of the respondent, started living in rented accommodation alongwith her daughter in 2011 as the respondent has deserted her.

It is further alleged that Eric Franklin brother of the respondent prevented access of the aggrieved to the flat of her father in law, who is now deceased and who had died intestate, and she claims to have a right in the same.

It has been alleged that the respondent abused and tortured the aggrieved without any rhyme and reason and that he also threatened her with dire consequences if she filed any complaint against him in any police station or in court of law.
5. It is alleged that the respondent does not provide money for maintaining the aggrieved or her daughter (who studies in Holy Child Auxillium School) neither looks after her medical needs.
It is also alleged that he also does not provide any food, clothes, shelter etc. to the aggrieved, hence the present case.

6. Notice of the applications was issued to respondent who did not appear despite service and appeared on 03.10.2012 only subsequent to issuance of bailable warrants against him by the Ld Predecessor of this court.
7.

In his reply as filed on 08.04.2013, the respondent raised preliminary objection that the aggrieved was employed for gain and CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 3 of 10 hence could maintain herself.

entities.text: CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 3 of 10
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has not disputed the factum of his marriage with the aggrieved nor has he disputed that he is not residing with the aggrieved since March 2011.
He has however attributed the quarrels to instigation and pressure by sister of the aggrieved i.e. Ms Krishna to purchase a house in the name of the aggrieved.
The allegations regarding extramarital affairs have been denied as have the allegations regarding miscarriage.
Rest of the averments and allegations have been denied on merits.
8. In the rejoinder as filed on 20.05.2013, the aggrieved denied the averments made by the respondent in the reply and reaffirmed the averments made in her application.

9. Domestic Incident Report was filed by the Protection officer on 21.08.2013.

However as respondent did not join the proceedings despite repeated calls, he was proceeded exparte on 21.08.2013 itself which order was set aside on 02.01.2014 subject to payment of costs which the respondent did not pay and he was again proceeded exparte on 25.07.2014 by the Ld Predecessor of this court.
10.

To prove her case, the aggrieved Lipika David led exparte complainant evidence and examined only herself as CW1 and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. CW1/1) and additional affidavit (Ex.CW1/2) on similar lines as her application and also proved the following documents:
birth certificate of her daughter Ex.CW1/A; Marriage certificate Ex.CW1/B; One Marriage photograph Ex.CW1/C; Receipt of money order Mark CW1/D, Copy of stitching bill dt. 5.4.2013 Mark CW1/E along with CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David

Ex.CW1/G was deexhibited as the aggrieved did not rely on the same.
11. Final arguments were advanced by the aggrieved herself.
12. I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submissions made during the course of final arguments and have carefully perused the entire evidence on record.

13. By virtue of Section 2(a), the reliefs under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 can be availed by a woman only if she is in a domestic relationship with the respondent and was subjected to domestic violence by the respondent.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 14. Section 2(f) of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 defines domestic relationship.

entities.text: Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The testimony of CW1 in respect of her being married to respondent on 20.11.2002 and that thereafter she was residing with her husband at rented house in Munirka has not been disputed by the respondent and hence being an admitted fact, the same need not be proved by further evidence.

Thus, from the admissions of the respondent as also her unrebutted oral testimony the aggrieved has proved that she was living with the respondent as wife of the respondent and was living together with him in a shared household / matrimonial home.

Hence the factum of domestic relationship between the aggrieved and the respondent has CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh.
Victor David Page No. 5 of 10 been proved.

sentences.text: 15. In respect of the infliction of the domestic violence, the testimony of CW1 and the documents relied upon by her have gone unrebutted.
Despite opportunities the respondent for reasons best known to him chose not to join the present proceedings to controvert any evidence led by the aggrieved.
Thus the averments of the aggrieved as also her testimony in her evidence by way of affidavit are deemed to be admitted by the respondent as it has remained unchallenged and unrebutted.
Further, no reason has been brought on record to disbelieve the uncontroverted evidence led by the aggrieved.

Accordingly, by unrebutted testimony, the aggrieved has been able to prove that the respondent has committed certain acts of physical and economic violence against the Cc No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David vs . Sh. Victor David Page No. 1 Of 10 on 7 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28340180/

aggrieved and thus, as the aggrieved person has been able to prove the domestic violence committed upon her, she is entitled to claim reliefs under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondent. sentences.text: Aggrieved has prayed for any protection order by prohibiting the respondent from communicating with the aggrieved as also directions against him to stay away from her and other relatives of the aggrieved to prohibit violence against them.

No evidence has been led by the aggrieved that since she started residing separately from her husband, he has contacted her or her CC No: 258/1 Smt.
Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 6 of 10 relatives in any manner and hence, the said relief appears to be vague in nature.

However, keeping in view that certain acts of domestic violence have been committed upon the aggrieved in the past which resulted in the present matter, and to further ensure safety and security of the aggrieved, I deem it fit to pass a protection order in favour of the aggrieved whereby the respondent is restrained from communicating, in any manner whatsoever,
with the aggrieved and her relatives until further orders.

Any default in compliance of this order shall entail a liability Under Section 31 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act 17. Residence Order Under Section 19 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act: The aggrieved has prayed for residence orders to the effect that respondent be ordered to pay the rent of the premises where the aggrieved is residing as per the status of the respondent.

sentences.text: As per the evidence led by the aggrieved herself it has been proved that the aggrieved is not residing at her matrimonial/shared household since 2011 despite having a right to reside therein being the wife of the respondent.

It is duly noted that the aggrieved has neither pleaded nor proved that the flat of her father in law was her shared household at any point of time nor has she sought to be reinstated in her matrimonial/shared household.

Thus, keeping in view that the aggrieved is living separately with her minor daughter and that she would require certain monetary relief for paying rent for alternate accommodation, therefore, I deem it fit to award a sum of Rs.2,500/ per month as rent including water CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 7 of 10 and electricity charges payable to the aggrieved by the respondent husband for arranging an alternate accommodation as in his income affidavit the respondent has claimed to be paying Rs. 2,500/ per month as rent including water and electricity.

18. Monetary Reliefs Under Section 20 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act:

The aggrieved has prayed for a sum of Rs. 15,000/ per month towards basic necessity including food,
clothes, household expenses etc; Rs. 10,000/ towards medical expenses and a further sum of Rs.
20,000/ towards loss/physical /mental injury for the total sum of Rs. 45,000/.
19.

As per the settled law, the aggrieved as well as her children are entitled to get monetary relief which is adequate, fair, reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
In her evidence CW1/1, the aggrieved has merely alleged that the respondent is working as an AC mechanic and had earned a substantial amount of money when he had gone to work abroad.
She has not led any evidence to prove the quantum of earning of the respondent at the time of filing of the application or any time prior or subsequent thereto.

2. opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. By virtue of Section 2(a), the reliefs under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 can be availed by a woman only if she is in a domestic relationship with the respondent and was subjected to domestic violence by the respondent.
14. Section 2(f) of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 defines domestic relationship.
The testimony of CW1 in respect of her being married to respondent on 20.11.2002 and that thereafter she was residing with her husband at rented house in Munirka has not been disputed by the respondent and hence being an admitted fact, the same need not be proved by further evidence.
Thus, from the admissions of the respondent as also her unrebutted oral testimony the aggrieved has proved that she was living with the respondent as wife of the respondent and was living together with him in a shared household / matrimonial home.
15. In respect of the infliction of the domestic violence, the testimony of CW1 and the documents relied upon by her have gone unrebutted.
Despite opportunities the respondent for reasons best known to him chose not to join the present proceedings to controvert any evidence led by the aggrieved.
Thus the averments of the aggrieved as also her testimony in her evidence by way of affidavit are deemed to be admitted by the respondent as it has remained unchallenged and unrebutted.
Further, no reason has been brought on record to disbelieve the uncontroverted evidence led by the aggrieved.
aggrieved and thus, as the aggrieved person has been able to prove the domestic violence committed upon her, she is entitled to claim reliefs under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondent. Reliefs 16. Protection Order Under Section 18 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act:
Any default in compliance of this order shall entail a liability Under Section 31 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act 17. Residence Order Under Section 19 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act: The aggrieved has prayed for residence orders to the effect that respondent be ordered to pay the rent of the premises where the aggrieved is residing as per the status of the respondent.
As per the evidence led by the aggrieved herself it has been proved that the aggrieved is not residing at her matrimonial/shared household since 2011 despite having a right to reside therein being the wife of the respondent.
Thus, keeping in view that the aggrieved is living separately with her minor daughter and that she would require certain monetary relief for paying rent for alternate accommodation, therefore, I deem it fit to award a sum of Rs.2,500/ per month as rent including water CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 7 of 10 and electricity charges payable to the aggrieved by the respondent husband for arranging an alternate accommodation as in his income affidavit the respondent has claimed to be paying Rs. 2,500/ per month as rent including water and electricity.
As per the settled law, the aggrieved as well as her children are entitled to get monetary relief which is adequate, fair, reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
Thus, the relief under Section 21 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act is declined.
